audit.why: Packet win rate is 62.5 over 16 games. Small sample, but it is the stored figure and it points the same way as the content layer's narrative.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this HARD, 8/10 difficulty, and marks every one of the seven phases 'Wukong'. The content layer calls it [Skill,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill] and its prose says 'This is your lane'. The stored win rate is 62.5.
audit.why: The full layer is internally contradictory: every phase side says Wukong while every phase 'why' underneath describes Mel winning ('Q volleys win every level-1 range war', 'your core chunk'). Sides and text disagree, the two layers disagree, and both disagree with a 62.5 win rate. An 8/10 HARD rating cannot be right for a matchup Mel wins more often than not.
audit.corrected: Moved diff to EVEN, difficulty to 6/10, Wukong carry threat to 7.5/10, tone to the amber EVEN colour. The seven phases[].side values still read 'Wukong' and need a human pass — a Wukong->Mel or Wukong->Skill swap cannot satisfy the +/-10% length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report Key Ability Interactions all call Nimbus Strike 'his only gap-close'.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is also a dash — Wukong becomes invisible and dashes while leaving a clone behind. Telling the player Nimbus Strike's downtime is a safe window is actively dangerous, because he can still cross ground on W, invisibly, and open from an angle she is not watching.
audit.corrected: Named Warrior Trickster as a second entry tool and gave both real cooldowns (Nimbus Strike 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7, Warrior Trickster 22/21/20/19/18).
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (dash flag on W and E)

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why says Rebuttal's reflect 'turns his poke into your poke', and full.tldr says 'his dash goes through your reflect'.
audit.why: Wukong has no projectile on any slot — Stone Skin, Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone are all non-projectile. Rebuttal's reflect has nothing to send back in this matchup, so its entire value here is the damage prevention and the move speed. A player told to 'hold the reflect for his real spell' will hold it waiting for a spell that never comes.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[1].why and tldr around Rebuttal as pure damage immunity, spent on the Cyclone burst.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (no projectile flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Solar Snare's root denies Wukong's dashes, and content.early tells the player to 'root him on the dash'.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike and Warrior Trickster are both dash-class movement abilities, and a rooted champion cannot cast a dash. That makes the root a pre-emptive denial, not a reaction. Rooting him mid-dash does nothing — the advice as written teaches the player to react a beat too late every single time.
audit.corrected: Reframed every root line as 'root before he commits' and stated that a rooted Wukong casts neither dash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (dash flag on W and E)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike is treated as though it must target Mel.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike dashes to a targeted enemy — that includes minions. Wukong routinely dashes to a caster minion in the wave to halve the gap and then walks the rest, which means the spacing a 550-range Mel thinks is safe is really 650 units shorter than she believes whenever the wave is between them.
audit.corrected: Added the minion-target entry to breakdown.cooldowns, content.early and wants.foe[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (E Nimbus Strike: dashes to a targeted enemy)

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a burned Nimbus Strike a 'fifteen-second invitation'. tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7 seconds — ten at rank 1, not fifteen. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 — thirty-eight at rank 1, not twenty. Both errors point the same wrong way: they make Mel's punish window look longer and her mistake look cheaper than either really is.
audit.corrected: Replaced both with the real figures and put Cyclone's 130/110/90 into the cooldown block, which previously carried no numbers at all.

audit.why: The existing claim that his armour stacking does nothing against Mel is right — Stone Skin gives stacking armour and Crushing Blow shreds armour, and Mel deals magic damage on every slot. I only attached the real ability names to it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (P Stone Skin, Q Crushing Blow)

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow's auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Crushing Blow is an auto-reset that also extends his attack range by up to 100 units at rank 5. The tell for his burst is the wind-up on that attack, not a visible ability cast, and the extra range means his threat circle is bigger than his idle auto range suggests.
audit.corrected: Named the Crushing Blow reset inside the all-in chain in spikes[3].text and content.late.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely even — he can sit out of your single-ability range and you can't commit yet, so just hit Radiant Volley on the wave and farm. The lane flips at 2: Q plus Solar Snare means when he walks up for a CS, you land the root and start banking Overwhelm stacks he can't trade back through. By 3 you have your W barrier up too, so if he tries to E-dash in to start a fight, root him on the dash and W to negate the follow-up burst — his armor stacking is meaningless against your magic kit.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even — he can sit out of your single-ability range and you can't commit yet, so just hit Radiant Volley on the wave and farm. The lane flips at 2: Q plus Solar Snare means when he walks up for a CS, you land the root and start banking Overwhelm stacks he can't trade back through. Watch for Nimbus Strike targeting a minion to halve the gap first — root him before he commits, because a rooted Wukong cannot dash at all, and Stone Skin's armour is meaningless against your magic kit.

edits.before: This is your lane. Your Q cooldown drops and Overwhelm stacks pile up every time he steps into range, so poke him low and respect only one thing: his E-dash-into-R knockup is his entire all-in, and it's on a long cooldown. Bait it with spacing, and the moment he commits E onto you, clamp Solar Snare's root and detonate with Golden Eclipse — at 6 your built-up stacks plus R can flat execute a diving Wukong from range. Watch the W clone juke: don't blow your root on the decoy or you give him a free window.
edits.after: This is your lane. Your Q cooldown drops and Overwhelm stacks pile up every time he steps into range, so poke him low and respect only one thing: Nimbus Strike into Cyclone is his entire all-in, and Cyclone is 130 seconds at rank 1. Bait it with spacing, and the moment he has committed onto you, clamp Solar Snare's root and detonate with Golden Eclipse — at 6 your built-up stacks plus R can flat execute a diving Wukong from range. Don't blow the root on a Warrior Trickster clone, or you hand him the window.

edits.before: You stay strong into him as long as he can't one-shot the dive — your infinitely-scaling passive keeps your poke and execute relevant, and W still eats his engage burst. The danger is the all-in math flipping: a fed Wukong with cooldowns up can E-dash in, chain his Q-empowered hits and R knockup, and burst your squishy frame before R comes back. Keep Flash for his E commit, never face-check brush where his clone can hide the engage, and play around your team — you win the poke war but lose the coinflip if he lands the full chain with no peel.
edits.after: You stay strong into him as long as he can't one-shot the dive — your infinitely-scaling passive keeps your poke and execute relevant, and W still eats his engage burst. The danger is the all-in math flipping: a fed Wukong with cooldowns up can Nimbus Strike in, chain a Crushing Blow reset and Cyclone's knockup, and burst your squishy frame before R comes back. notes: PHASE SIDES ARE BROKEN (needs a human): all seven full.phases[].side values for mel/wukong read 'Wukong', while the 'why' text sitting under each one describes Mel winning ('Q volleys win every level-1 range war', 'Full kit: E snare into full Q volleys is your core chunk'). content.win for the same matchup is [Skill,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill]. This looks like a generation fault rather than a judgement call. I corrected diff/diffRating/carryRating/tone to EVEN 6/10 to match the 62.5 win rate and the content narrative, but I could not touch the side values: a 'Wukong' (6 chars) to 'Mel' (3) or 'Skill' (5) swap cannot pass the +/-10% length band. Recommend [Skill,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill] in both layers. REFLECT IS DEAD HERE: Wukong has no projectile on any slot, so Rebuttal's reflect does nothing in this matchup — the old text sold it twice (tldr and phases[1].why) and told the player to hold W waiting for a spell that never comes. KIT FLAG NOTE: mel.json flags W Rebuttal with 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'; Riot's own description mentions no terrain, only a barrier that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed. I did not build any advice on Rebuttal physically blocking Nimbus Strike. SUSPECTNAMES FALSE POSITIVE: the packet flags "Solar Snare's" as a probable wrong name; Solar Snare is Mel's real E and this is just the possessive.
